Definition: from the base of G5176; a he-goat (as a gnawer):--goat.
BiblicalUsage: Hebrews says it was not by the blood of goats and calves but by His own blood that Christ entered once into the holy place. Hebrews says it was not by the blood of goats and calves but by His own blood that He entered once into the holy place, and that the blood of bulls and goats sanctified only to the purifying of the flesh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Hebrews turns on the contrast: the blood of goats could only wash the outside, and only His own blood could enter in and obtain redemption.
